html:
SMTO-EML-0018 — One of the email addresses isn't valid

GUID: 0ba07a7d-52e5-538c-8f5d-ce1e08b204d7
Slug: email-recipient-invalid
Domain: EML · Subsystem: email-smtp

What happened

  • An address in the To, Cc or Bcc list isn't written as a complete email address, so SMTO stopped before sending. Nothing was sent.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Technical details in this panel to see which list, To, Cc or Bcc, has the problem. The details name the list without showing the address itself.
  2. Check each address in that list has exactly one @, no spaces, and a full domain such as example.com. A name on its own, or two addresses run together, isn't a valid address.
  3. Ask SMTO to send the email again with the corrected addresses. Nothing was sent, so sending the corrected email won't create a duplicate.

What success looks like

  • SMTO reports the mail server accepted the message for your recipients.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. This is about how the email was written, not your email account, so don't change your password or reconnect the account because of it.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Recipient validation rejected a to, cc or bcc value that was not a list, or a mailbox address that was malformed, over 320 characters, contained control characters, or had an invalid domain.

What this means

  • A recipient list or mailbox address is invalid. The producer identifies the failed field or preparation stage without exposing private values.

Why this can happen

  • Recipient validation rejects the list or a mailbox address.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the reported field, failure phase and retained receipt before choosing a correction.

How to fix it

  • Read the field fact (to, cc or bcc) and correct that argument to a list of single addr-spec mailboxes: one @, a valid local part, an LDH or IDNA domain, at most 320 characters, no control characters.
  • Correct the indicated to, cc or bcc field using a list of valid mailbox addresses.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the reported condition first. Retry only when existing execution and effect evidence permits it; reconcile an uncertain prior send.

How to verify the fix

  • All requested recipient lists and addresses validate.

What not to do

  • Do not infer an authentication rejection from local validation. Preserve the recorded execution and delivery evidence before any retry.

Technical notes

  • Do not infer an authentication rejection from local validation. Preserve the recorded execution and delivery evidence before any retry.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
